content:
# 1 Maccabees Chapter 10 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Verses:** 89 | **Disagreements:** 44

---

## Summary
Chapter 10 is dominated by embedded political documents (Demetrius's privileges letter, vv.25-45) and court scenes. Disagreements concentrate on diplomatic vocabulary, the letter's tax terminology, and narrative descriptors.

---

## Disagreements

**v.1** — "came up and took possession" (EMET) vs. "came up and seized" (LOGOS) vs. "sailed in, took the port of" (PNEUMA) — PNEUMA adds "sailed in" and "port of" for geographic clarity.

**v.3** — "with words of peace" (EMET) vs. "conciliatory words" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "a friendly letter, designed to flatter" (PNEUMA) — register divergence from formal to paraphrase.

**v.4** — "Let us make haste" (EMET) vs. "We must act before" (LOGOS) vs. "We need to make a deal" (PNEUMA) vs. "Let us act quickly" (SOPHIA) — idiom range.

**v.6** — "furnish arms" (EMET) vs. "produce weapons" (LOGOS) vs. "arm troops" (PNEUMA) vs. "furnish weapons" (SOPHIA)

**v.8** — "give him authority to gather troops" — all agree; PNEUMA simplifies to "raise an army."

**v.11** — "hewn stones" (EMET) vs. "dressed stone" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "dressed stone" (PNEUMA) — EMET retains a more archaic term.

**v.16** — "Shall we find another man like him? And now let us" (EMET) vs. "Shall we ever find another man like him? We must" (LOGOS) — LOGOS adds "ever" for rhetorical force.

**v.20** — "purple robe and a golden crown" — all agree; PNEUMA renders as "purple robe and a gold crown" (omits definite article before gold).

**v.20** — appointment formula: "you shall be called the king's friend" (EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "You shall bear the title Friend of the King" (PNEUMA) — formalized vs. capitalized title.

**v.21** — "holy garments" (EMET) vs. "sacred vestments" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "priestly vestments" (PNEUMA)

**v.21** — Date notation: EMET gives the formal regnal year; PNEUMA converts to "152 BCE" — SOPHIA retains regnal year throughout.

**v.22** — "was grieved" (EMET) vs. "was distressed" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "felt the sting of it" (PNEUMA)

**v.23** — "gotten ahead of us in making friendship with the Jews" (EMET) vs. "outmaneuvered us in winning the friendship" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.25** — Letter format: all translators reproduce the formal epistolary greeting but differ in paragraph structure within the letter.

**v.29** — "salt-tax" (EMET, hyphenated) vs. "salt tax" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA, not hyphenated)
- "crown-levies" (EMET) vs. "crown levies" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "crown taxes" (PNEUMA)

**v.30** — "the third of the grain and the half of the fruit of trees" (EMET) vs. "one-third of the grain harvest and one-half of the fruit" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA clarify "harvest."

**v.31** — "holy and free from tithe and levy" (EMET) vs. "holy and exempt from taxation" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "sacred and tax-exempt" (PNEUMA)

**v.32** — "I remit my authority over the citadel" (EMET) vs. "I surrender my authority" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — "surrender" preferred over "remit" as more politically charged.

**v.33** — "without payment" (EMET) vs. "without ransom" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — "ransom" more specific to a captive context.

**v.34** — "days of exemption and freedom" (EMET) vs. "days of immunity and freedom" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "days of full legal immunity" (PNEUMA)

**v.36** — "allowances be given to them as to all the king's forces" (EMET) vs. "with pay equal to all royal troops" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "with full pay and benefits, equal to any other soldier" (PNEUMA)

**v.38** — "reckoned to be under one rule" (EMET) vs. "placed under a single authority" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "answerable only to the high priest" (PNEUMA — anticipates v.38b in v.38a)

**v.39** — "as a gift to the sanctuary" (EMET) vs. "as an endowment to the Jerusalem sanctuary" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "I donate to the Jerusalem temple" (PNEUMA)

**v.41** — "surplus that the officials had not paid" (EMET) vs. "arrears that officials have failed to pay" (SOPHIA) vs. "back payments that royal officials owe" (PNEUMA)

**v.42** — "used to take from the income of the sanctuary" (EMET) vs. "taken annually from temple income" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) — minor structural difference.

**v.43** — "whatever their debt or their obligation" (EMET) vs. "whatever their debt or obligation" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) — minor article difference.

**v.46** — "gave no credence to them nor accepted them" (EMET) vs. "put no stock in them and did not accept them" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "paid it no mind" (PNEUMA) — PNEUMA most informal.

**v.47** — "all their days" (EMET) vs. "for the rest of his days" (LOGOS) vs. "for good" (PNEUMA) — EMET preserves the Semitic idiom; LOGOS clarifies antecedent.

**v.50** — "fell on that day" (EMET/LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "Demetrius was dead" (PNEUMA) — PNEUMA's flat finality is a stylistic choice.

**v.51** — "ambassadors" (EMET) vs. "envoys" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.60** — "with pomp" (EMET) vs. "in state" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.61** — "pestilent men of Israel, lawless men" (EMET) vs. "scoundrels from Israel, troublemakers" (LOGOS) vs. "troublemakers — Jewish renegades" (PNEUMA) vs. "troublemakers from Israel — lawless men" (SOPHIA) — the Greek ἄνδρες λοιμοί; strong pejorative.

**v.65** — "chief friends" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "principal friends" (LOGOS) vs. "principal friends" (PNEUMA) — court rank term.

**v.67** — PNEUMA converts regnal year to "147 BCE"; others retain the regnal year format.

**v.69** — "laughingstock and a reproach" (EMET) vs. "object of ridicule and mockery" (LOGOS) vs. "laughingstock of me" (PNEUMA) vs. "laughingstock and a reproach" (SOPHIA)

**v.72** — "your fathers were twice put to flight" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "your ancestors were twice driven to flight" (LOGOS) vs. "your own ancestors were routed twice" (PNEUMA)

**v.73** — "neither stone nor flint" (EMET) vs. "no stone, no rock" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) vs. "no stone, no cliff" (PNEUMA) — different renderings of the Greek πέτρα.

**v.77** — "as if he was on his way through" (EMET) vs. "as if simply passing through" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — slight structural difference.

**v.80** — "shot arrows at the people from morning until evening" (EMET) vs. "pelted with arrows from morning till evening" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.83** — "Beth-dagon the temple of their idol" (EMET/SOPHIA) vs. "the temple of Dagon — their idol" (LOGOS) vs. "the temple of Dagon — their god" (PNEUMA) — PNEUMA's "god" is arguably more neutral than "idol."

**v.86** — "with great pomp" (EMET) vs. "with great ceremony" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA)

**v.89** — "golden buckle" (EMET) vs. "golden clasp" (LOGOS/SOPHIA/PNEUMA) — Greek πόρπη; SOPHIA chose "clasp" as more formal.
